sentences.text: Rugops was a medium-sized dinosaur reaching approximately 4.4 meters in length with a skull measuring about 31.5 centimeters long.
Its head featured a unique arrangement of two rows of seven holes on the top, while the snout likely possessed an armor-like layer of skin beneath the scales.
This species possesses two unique derived characters that distinguish it from all other known dinosaurs.
Like its relatives, Rugops likely had very short arms or even vestigial limbs that were too small to be useful for grasping.
Depressions on the nasal bones may have anchored sensory structures or soft tissues used for visual display, similar to the scales found on modern crocodiles and lizards.
Paul Sereno suggested that the animal might have been a scavenger because its head was not built for fighting or crushing bones.
The species Rugops primus was formally described in 2004 by Paul Sereno, Jeffrey Wilson, and Jack Conrad based on a partial skull discovered in 2000.
Finding this skull in Niger was crucial for understanding theropod evolution and proved the landmass was still connected to Gondwana at that time.
Delcourt proposed that the armor-like dermis on the head may have been used for low-motion headbutting behavior.
This predator lived alongside other large theropods such as Carcharodontosaurus iguidensis, Spinosaurus, and Deltadromeus.
Rugops is classified within the family Abelisauridae and is considered a basal representative of that group.
Multiple analyses have recovered it as the most basal abelisaurid, separate from South American forms, Brachyrostra, and the Majungasaurinae of India, Madagascar, and Europe.
The type species, Rugops primus, means 'first wrinkled face' and is thought to be phylogenetically related to Majungasaurus.
Rugops lived during the Cenomanian stage, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
Fossils were found in the Echkar Formation, which dates to around 96 million years ago, in a fluvial and lacustrine environment with humid or semi-arid conditions.
Some studies place Rugops as more derived than Rahiolisaurus and Eoabelisaurus but more basal than other abelisaurids.
